_comment: Benchmark written and frozen BEFORE the scorer was implemented. EXACT cases are generated from catalogue text by run_eval.py (lowercased, punctuation stripped). expected = acceptable review tiers.

queries.text: Ishaan, who will inherit his father's skyscraper developer business, hides his wealth and starts driving a car for the family of Naira, the girl he is engaged to, because he wants to know if she wants him or his bank balance. Her relatives look down on him as a poor hired hand, and her dad shames him before a room full of visitors. Naira refuses to leave his side and secretly covers the made-up loans he claims to owe. The night of their engagement celebration, her dad's business is going under and a lender dispatches an unknown backer. Ishaan arrives in that backer's seat, announces who he really is to the whole crowd and rescues the company. Her father grovels, while Naira weighs whether she can forgive being deceived.

Kavya enters a marriage on paper with Samar, who cooks at a street-side ramen cart, because her grandmother is very ill and wishes to see her wed. Samar is ridiculed by her mother and her aunts at every gathering, and they urge Kavya to leave him. Without a word, Samar settles the unpaid rent the relatives owe. When the owner of the property serves the entire household an eviction warning, we learn Samar secretly holds the title to the building. At dinner he rips the warning and says he is the owner. Kavya sees that the arrangement on paper has grown into something real, and her mother has to say sorry to a ramen cook.

On their wedding day, Diya's fiance Aman disappears with her little sister Pihu, leaving her standing at the mandap. Facing the stunned crowd, Diya asks Aman's wealthy uncle Mr. Khanna to marry her instead, and he agrees. At the Khanna mansion, Aman and Pihu are forced to address her as their aunt. Diya collects documents showing the pair drained her dead mother's savings account. During the family's yearly celebration she runs the documents on the big screen in the hall. The two are evicted, and Diya finds out the real reason the uncle accepted.

Her husband Varun and her closest friend Sheetal burn the family home with Anjali inside, to get hold of her wealth. Anjali opens her eyes three years earlier, on the day of her betrothal. Armed with memory of the future, she rewrites her will in secret and records the two scheming. She skips the betrothal and, on the day of the blaze, gets her relatives out of the house. When the arsonists strike, the building is empty, and investigators link the fire to Varun. Sheetal talks to protect herself, and Anjali gets the life that was stolen from her.

A girl from a shanty, Pooja, learns from a genetic test that nurses switched her with the baby of a wealthy household soon after the two were born. The wealthy household takes her in yet regards her as a disgrace and keeps doting on the daughter they had raised, Aisha. Aisha had known the secret for years and concealed the lab report. Pooja locates the maternity ward records showing Aisha's mother bribed a nurse to switch the infants. At the family's fundraising dinner, she exposes the records. The wealthy matriarch has to admit before everyone that she picked the wrong daughter.

A road accident erases Fiza's memory. Her husband's girlfriend Rhea persuades her she is merely a domestic servant and gets her to mop floors. Under a loose plank, Fiza finds a journal with the truth about her life. As her memory returns she keeps up the act of confusion. At her husband's fundraiser she enters as the mistress of the house and plays the lies the girlfriend had recorded. The husband sees how he was fooled, and Rhea is thrown out.

During the ceremony under the full moon, pack leader Ryker declares in public that he rejects his destined mate Selene, saying she is feeble since she cannot transform. Exiled from her pack, Selene stumbles into the hills. A fading elder wolf tells her she descends from the Moon Goddess and her strength is stirring. When feral wolves raid Ryker's territory, he is helpless. Selene comes back, becomes a white wolf and routs them. Ryker pleads with her to take him back and she resolves to refuse.

Naveen, who works under head cook Shalini, takes her private kebab formula and uses it to win a TV cooking showdown. Shalini loses her job and begins selling kebabs from a roadside cart. A food blogger posts a clip of her stall that blows up overnight. Naveen's kitchen can't recreate the secret spice. Shalini dares him to a live cooking duel before a studio crowd. She prevails and starts her own eatery.

Sister Mehr is pressured to stand in for her sister Noor, who fled before her wedding to tycoon Aarav. Mehr puts on the gown and plays the part at the groom's palace. She learns Noor escaped to avoid owing money to a loan shark. Aarav grows doubtful as Mehr acts nothing like the woman he knew. He challenges her in the courtyard and she tells him all. Aarav clears the loan shark's claim and then asks Mehr to marry him for real.

A terminally ill business magnate sets a competition between his three grandkids for control of his group. Two wealthy ones spend a month fighting and paying off the solicitor. The poorest grandchild, Maya, just comes by each night and reads aloud to him. A buried clause in his testament says the successor must be whoever stayed by his side. When he passes, the solicitor reads the clause. Maya gets it all and puts her cousins on payroll.

Billionaire Rudra pretends to be a poor gardener so that he can get inside a rival family's estate and find the missing deed to his grandfather's farmland. The family's son bullies him and orders him to dig up the lawn. Rudra finds the deed in a locked greenhouse and carries it to court, where the judge rules in his favour and returns the land to the village.

CEO Vedant disguises himself as a struggling tutor to teach the daughter of a rival family. The relatives insult his clothes and refuse to let him eat at their table. Vedant keeps teaching the shy girl until she passes her board exams. At the school fair he reveals that he owns the town's only school and announces that tuition will be free for every child.

Mina and Joy sign a fake marriage contract so that they can adopt an orphaned boy they both love, since the agency only gives children to married couples. A social worker visits unannounced and they must pretend to be a loving couple. The court grants the adoption, and they stay friends and raise the boy as co-parents.

After her husband leaves her for a younger colleague, Sheela moves to a hill station and opens a small bookshop. She falls in love with Hari, the local carpenter who builds her shelves. Her ex-husband travels up the mountain to ask for a second chance. He finds her laughing with Hari, and quietly drives home.

Baker Mira is betrayed by her business partner and fiance, who sells her shop behind her back and leaves her with nothing. She rebuilds a bakery from a rented kitchen under a new name and wins the city's best customers. The partner's chain of stores starts losing money. Mira buys his company through a trust, and when he comes begging for a job she hands him an apron.

Fifteen-year-old Kunal is reborn into his younger body after dying at forty. He decides not to chase money but to spend time with his father, who died when Kunal was twenty. They repair an old scooter together and fish at the lake. When the day of his father's heart attack comes, Kunal calls the ambulance in time.

Famous detective Mohan loses his memory after a fall in his study. Using only his own handwritten case notebook he has to work out who killed his mentor. The trail leads through three old clients and an auction house. He finally realises that the mentor wrote the note that framed a junior policeman, and takes the evidence to the commissioner.

At the Moonridge academy for young werewolves, pup Zara is the smallest student and is picked last for every team. She enters the annual wolf tournament as a joke and loses the first round badly. A retired coach trains her to use speed instead of strength. In the final she beats the school champion and the academy raises its cup for her.

Neha discovers she is pregnant after a single night with a stranger at a conference and decides to keep the baby. She builds a small bakery that survives on a loan. A famous food critic reviews her bakery and gives it five stars without knowing he is the baby's father. When her daughter is born he arrives for another review and sees the baby's eyes.

Nurse Beena works in a public hospital that is going to be closed by the state. She convinces the staff to run night clinics on the pavement and organises a crowdfunding page for new equipment. The local newspaper covers the campaign and the minister visits. The hospital stays open and gets a new wing.

On the morning of their arranged wedding, bride Pallavi and groom Sid discover that each is secretly in love with someone else. They agree to stage a fake quarrel over the dowry so both families will cancel the ceremony. The plan nearly fails when the priests try to reconcile them. In the end both marry the people they love, and the two families become business partners.

A landowner leaves each of his four children a farm in his will. The siblings quarrel over water rights, and the eldest builds a fence across the stream. A long drought dries up every well but one on the youngest sister's land. The four of them dig a shared canal together, and the fence is pulled down.

Engineer Lia wakes up alone on a space station after a meteor strike cuts all contact with Earth. She repairs the oxygen recycler, then finds that the station's computer has been editing the logs. She builds a radio from spare parts and calls a passing freighter. The freighter's crew arrives to rescue her before the air runs out.

A small village cricket team has lost every match for ten years. A retired army cook becomes their coach and makes them practise by catching sacks of flour. The team reaches the district final by luck. They lose again, but the whole village celebrates with a feast.

A family moves into a cheap old house where the lights flicker every night at three. The youngest son talks to a boy nobody else can see. They find a sealed room with a child's drawings of a flood. The family helps the ghost find his lost sister's grave and the house falls quiet.

Four college friends go trekking in the Himalayas and get cut off by a landslide. They share a single tent, ration their food and argue about which route to take. One of them breaks a leg and the others take turns carrying her. A helicopter finds them on the fifth day.

Shy teenager Omkar builds a water filter from clay pots for the school science fair. His friends laugh and the judges ignore his table until a power cut stops every other exhibit. Only his filter keeps working. The state education board funds him to install them in twenty villages.

Captain Arav is blamed for a plane accident that was really caused by his co-pilot Captain Soni, who altered a checklist. Arav's licence is cancelled. He flies cargo planes over the mountains under a different name. A dying engineer gives him an old flight recorder that holds the cockpit audio. He sends the audio to the aviation authority during a live press briefing. Soni is arrested and Arav is offered his seat back.

At the full moon ceremony, Alpha Dax publicly rejects his fated mate Nova because she is a late bloomer who cannot shift. She is banished and starts a quiet new life as a village vet. Years later Dax falls gravely ill and the pack healers cannot help him. Nova heals him with herbs and leaves before he wakes up. Dax searches for her and they talk for the first time as equals.

Hotel owner's daughter Kiara works as a waitress in her father's hotel under a false name. The head chef, Imran, passes off her menu ideas as his own and shouts at her in the kitchen. Kiara keeps dated notes of every recipe she proposes. At the hotel's grand reopening Imran presents her menu. Kiara walks on stage, reads her notes and announces that she is the owner's daughter.

Daughter-in-law Bhavna is scolded and ordered about by her father-in-law Gopal, who finds fault with everything she does. She takes it quietly for her husband's sake. The family lawyer reveals that Gopal has been secretly testing who deserves to run the family trust. When the will is read, Gopal names Bhavna as trustee because she never complained or cheated. Her brothers-in-law protest. Gopal pats her head.

Dev was bullied at school by Kunal and left town in shame. Years later he returns for the reunion as a famous venture investor. Kunal, now a failing shop owner, sneers at him before he realises who Dev is. Dev offers Kunal's whole street a place in his new mall. Kunal begs for a stall. Dev forgives him and makes him manager of the mall.
